variant-first.note: Set B binds more distinct facts correctly and keeps needed conditions (e.g., BASE CABINET quantity 1 tied to its dimensions, WATERCLOSET model tied to tag WC), and it adds correct millwork, revision and finish data that A omits. baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the main region behavior (blade pitch 0° in Region 2, TSR falling from ~20 at 3 m/s to ~3 at 25 m/s, 15 MW rated power, CP ≈ 0.5 in Region 2) and both recycle several claims verbatim. Set B additionally captures the printed Design Point CT = 0.804 and the blade pitch at 25 m/s (~23°), which Set A omits even though it repeats Design Point CP = 0.489 three times. Set A's main defect is three mutually inconsistent rotor-thrust values at 10 m/s (2.25, 2.8, and a "peak" 3.0 MN, when the curve peaks just under 3.00 MN near 10.5 m/s) plus 15 MW assigned to 10 m/s, while Set B's clear errors are the 10-RPM rotor speed at 10 m/s (the curve plateaus near 7.5 RPM) and a 22° pitch at 25 m/s contradicting its own 23° claim. On balance B covers more of the page's stated facts with slightly fewer misreadings.

Set B is less coherent on rotor thrust at 10 m/s, giving three mutually inconsistent values (2.25, 2.8, and a "peak" 3.0 MN that is really the axis maximum at ~10.5 m/s), while Set A's errors are a single misread rotor speed (10 RPM at 10 m/s instead of ~7.5) and a slightly inconsistent duplicate blade-pitch reading (22° vs 23° at 25 m/s).

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, sharing the same core claims (material properties from Table 4-1, 0.170 Hz first mode, 150 m hub height, 10 m monopile diameter, 30 m clearance with 120-m blades) and the same questionable items (a 0.18 Hz tower frequency that contradicts the stated 0.170 Hz, an invented 'steady-state' condition, and duplicated claims). Set A keeps the WISDEM/OpenFAST design condition on the material claim and uses a clean quote for the figure-derived frequency, while Set B drops that condition and appends a bracketed annotation ('[vertical line at ~0.17]') that is not document text. These differences are trivial, so the sets are effectively equivalent in correctness and coverage.

baseline-first.note: B captures two general-sheet-note facts that A omits — the A-511 Hardie installation reference and the tilt-and-turn door operation — whereas A only picks up the dotted-line door swing convention. Both sets are heavily redundant (finished floor, handrails, railing posts and tube count each repeated) and both give an unverifiable PV SOLAR ARRAY grid-line location. B's clear defects are the misbound 'W1 | dimension | 1.07' (1.07 is a window identifier) and the unsupported 'roof | component | PV SOLAR ARRAY' binding; A's only real fault is treating the 18'-0" solar-envelope height as a generic dimension.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the datum elevations (solar envelope 18'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", grade 0'-0"), the 2x4 cedar handrails, 1/8" cable railing, powdercoated steel flatbar railing posts, and the 2 x APSE-20 (40 tube) solar thermal array. Set A adds useful facts (A-511 Hardie reference, tilt-and-turn door operation, APSE-20 model, several window tags) but also introduces clear errors: it calls window tag 1.07 a "dimension" and binds PV solar array to a "roof" component, and its PV location (grid lines 4-5) is not supported by its quote. Set B is more disciplined, adding correct claims on cement fibre board siding, the dotted-line door swing convention, and tags D1 1.01 and W5 1.14, with only the unsupported PV grid-line location and a loose "dimension" label for the 18'-0" solar envelope height as defects. Both sets contain redundant repeats, but B has fewer misbound or unsupported claims while covering at least as many distinct facts.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the four Table 6-2 tower properties with faithful quotes and the damping condition (all modes, isolated tower without rotor-nacelle mass), and both contain three redundant restatements (height, CM location, mass). Neither set misreads or invents values, so the difference is small and turns on which redundancy is more informative.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the four Table 6-2 tower properties with accurate values, units and quotes, and both contain some duplication (CM location and integrated mass each appear twice). Set A's extra claim adds a genuinely distinct fact — the 1% critical damping specified in all modes of the isolated tower without rotor-nacelle mass — supported by the prose sentence. Set B's extra claim merely restates the 87.6 m height as 'overall height', a redundant/trivial duplicate of its own height claim, so A adds more correct information while B adds nothing new.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures more of the correctly bound hardware and lumber facts (hex through-bolt diameter and length, threaded rod diameter, plywood/reclaimed surface thickness and width, joist and frame sizes) with supporting quotes. Set B invents or misbinds several claims: an "overhang (left)" attribute for 4 1/4", a merged "nut sleeve" at 1" (the sheet lists 1" NUT and SLEVE separately), a "horizontal offset 1" condition on 1 1/2", and a fabricated entity "component E". variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core member sizes (2"x8" joist/frame, 3/4"x5 1/2" plywood deck and reclaimed wood surface, 3/8"x4" hex through bolt) and the 2'-4" first-floor-to-grade elevation. Set A, however, adds several unsupported or misbound claims: an invented 'overhang (left)' attribute for 4 1/4", an invented 'horizontal offset 1' condition for 1 1/2", a fabricated entity 'component E', the 1" nut dimension misbound to 'nut sleeve' (SLEVE is a separate label), and 3 1/2"/1'-0" attributed to 'C1 DECKING' when those dimensions belong to the B1 connection detail. Set B is cleaner, correctly splitting the 3/8"x4" bolt into length 4" and diameter 3/8" and adding the 3/4" threaded rod, though it repeats vague 'component 1' claims and also misassigns 8'-0" (a C3 footing-elevation dimension) to the decking footing plan. Both sets share the 8'-0" and 'C1 DECKING 3 1/2"' errors, but Set A accumulates more invented conditions and misbindings overall.

baseline-first.note: Set A's first claim is correct, but its second claim misbinds the 100 issues/concerns to the Draft Final Reports' 'number of findings' with a fragmentary quote, and its third claim wrongly treats 100 as the quantity of mission concepts (the text says four). Set B's three claims all correctly attribute the approximately 100 issues and concerns to the initial LCIT reviews across the four mission concepts, with full supporting quotes. B's claims are largely redundant restatements of one fact, but none are misread or invented, so B is more faithful overall.

baseline-first.note: Set B covers every fact on the page (HabEx, LUVOIR-A/B, Lynx, Origins diameters, instrument counts, starshade diameter, Lynx focal length) with values correctly bound to the named mission concepts and conditions such as on-axis/off-axis and flying in formation retained. Set A adds several vague or misbound claims — 'on-axis telescope', 'off-axis telescope', 'spacecraft' and 'grazing incidence mirror assembly' as entities, including the mirror assembly credited with three science instruments and a 10 m 'dimension' (actually Lynx's focal length) — plus many redundant duplicates of the same facts. The two sets are essentially identical in content: both capture the s-coordinate endpoints, the ontology definition standard, the composite layer definition, the flatback trailing-edge definition, and the damping values. Both make the same two errors — the edgewise damping is stated as 5% while the source says 3% (flapwise, edgewise, torsional = 3%, 3%, 6%), and both misbind the flatback midpoint definition to 'normalized arc length position' instead of the trailing edge. The only difference is phrasing of the composite-layer claim (A keeps 'following the curved blade reference axis' as a condition, B folds it into the value), which is immaterial.

variant-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical in content, differing only in ordering and in how the composite-layer definition is split (A keeps the full definition; B moves 'following the curved blade reference axis' into conditions, which is a minor but acceptable formatting choice). Both correctly capture the s-coordinate endpoints (0 at suction-side trailing edge, 1 at pressure-side trailing edge), the flatback trailing-edge definition, the IEA ontology standard, and the flapwise/torsional damping values. Both share the same errors: the first edgewise damping is given as 5% although the source states 3%, 3%, 6%, and the accompanying damping quotes are altered to '3%, 5%, and 6%'; both also include a nonsensical 'flatback surface | midpoint definition | normalized arc length position' claim with a garbled quote. Since the errors and correct claims are the same in both, neither is better.

Set A reads the leading-edge CarbonUD spike (~90 mm at 25% span) and the glass_uni trailing-edge stacks (~25 mm) at the right locations, whereas Set B misassigns the peak thicknesses to the Suction/Pressure sides (88/100 mm at invented s-coordinates) and puts 5 mm total at the LE where the stack actually peaks near 100 mm. B also invents numeric s-coordinate values (40, 60, 80) that the axes never state and reports an 11 mm glass_triax layer at 77% span that is only a thin band. Both sets share the same mid-span foam and total-thickness claims, but A's errors are mostly duplicated/contradictory glass_triax and CarbonUD values at 100% span plus one foam-at-TE misbinding, while B's are systematic misbindings of the plotted peaks. A therefore contains more correct, better-bound claims.

Both sets read a stacked bar chart and repeatedly bind total bar heights to the glass_biax segment (e.g. 38/42/32/28/22/18 mm), which are wrong since glass_biax is only the thin top segment (~1-5 mm). Set A adds three grossly misbound CarbonUD claims (13, 18 and 37 mm) where CarbonUD is only a thin sliver, plus three self-contradictory duplicate values for the same web/position/layer. Set B keeps the medium_density_foam series largely consistent with the large gray segments across positions and has fewer total-height misbindings and fewer internal contradictions. Neither set captures the small gelcoat/glass_triax/glass_uni layers, and both include trivial zero-thickness claims.

variant-first.note: Both sets read the stacked bar chart of layup layer thickness vs. span position and both contain values lifted from total bar heights and misbound to thin layers (e.g. glass_biax at 18–45 mm, when the pink layer is only a few mm thick). Set A is the more faithful of the two: it covers the dominant medium_density_foam layer for both web0 and web1 at several span positions with plausible values, and its errors are confined to glass_biax claims carrying total-thickness values. Set B additionally misbinds CarbonUD to 13, 18 and 37 mm values that cannot belong to that thin top layer, and gives almost no foam coverage for web1. Both sets contain internally contradictory near-duplicates (e.g. 3 vs 4 mm glass_biax at the same position) and neither quote is verbatim text from the page.
